 ..... Respondents
 Judgment

This is a petition filed u/s. 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act and Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules claiming for compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
On 18-7-2022 at about 12.30 p.m. when the petitioner was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-51-HT-3983 near Gownder service society,
Thirumagondanahalli, on Hosur-Bangalore NH 7 service road, at that time, driver of the Bolero vehicle No.KA-51- AB-4003 came in a rash and negligent manner on the opposite direction with high speed and came to the wrong side and dashed against the motor cycle, due to impact petitioner sustained grievous injuries and took treatment at hospital as inpatient.
Due to accidental injuries petitioner suffered disability and discomforts.
Hence prays to award compensation of rs.20 lakhs from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the Tribunal and filed written statement.
On the other hand, inspite of service of summons respondent No.1 remained absent and hence he was placed exparte.
4. The 2nd respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.

This respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of the offending vehicle and contended that the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
The driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
Further this respondent has denied the age, occupation and income, period of hospitalization and treatment taken by the petitioner.
It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The alleged accident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the rider of the motor cycle and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is high exorbitant.
Hence, on other grounds pray for dismissal of the petition.

5. From the above said pleadings three issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bulero van bearing reg.No.KA-51-AB-4003 on 18-7-2022 at about 12.30 p.m. at Hosur-Bengaluru NH 7 service road, near Karnataka gownder, service society,
Manoj vs Subramani on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41309102/
2 Thirumagondanahalli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru district ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
6.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P16 documents.
On the other hand, respondents have not led any defence evidence.

7. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 :

In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:

In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-4003, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 16 documents as Ex-P1 to 16 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report,
133 notice, reply notice, wound certificate, charge sheet, aadhaar card, discharge summary OPD case sheet, medical bills, prescriptions, advance receipt, CT scan report, CD, x-rays.
10.

On perusal of the evidence and materials on record, soon after the accident, petitioner himself has lodged the complaint against the driver of the Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-4003 as per Ex-P2.
Thereafter jurisdictional police have registered the FIR.

Thereafter the jurisdictional police station conducted a thorough and detailed investigation and filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle as per Ex- P8 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC by holding that on 18-7-2022 at about 12.30 p.m.in the Hosur-Bangalore NH 7 service road near Karnataka Gownder service society, accused drove his Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-4003 in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life from Chandapura and drove towards wrong side and hit to the petitioner who was coming from the opposite direction by riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-HT-3983, due to impact, petitioner sustained simple and grievous injuries.
It is pertinent to note here that respondent has not disputed the charge sheet and also not placed any evidence on record to held that charge sheet is collusive and defective.
Even the respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle has remained exparte.
Respondent No.2 insurance company has not examined either driver of the offending vehicle or any of the eye witness to disprove the evidence of the PW-1 and prove his contention.

Though PW-1 was Manoj vs Subramani on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41309102/
3 cross examined at length by the respondent No.1, except bare suggestion, respondent has not disputed the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Moreover PW-1 has outrightly denied the suggestion made by the respondent.

Apart from this, on perusal of Ex-P3 spot mahazar, it clearly shows that the spot of accident is NH 7 service road and the road was running from east to west and the width of the road is 25 feet and accident has been taken place at the southern side of the tar road.
Thus it clearly shows that accident has been taken place as the driver of the Bolero vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-51- AB-4003 has drove his vehicle on the wrong side of the road.
If at all the driver of the offending vehicle has not drove his vehicle to the right side of the road, accident has not been taken place.
Thus Ex-P3 clearly shows that accident had been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

It is pertinent to note here that neither of the respondent has not examined the driver of the offending vehicle who is a material witness to say about why he has drove his vehicle to the right side of the road.
Ex.P4 IMV report indicates that the occurrence of the said accident was not due to any of the mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident.

11. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
12. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
In view of above discussions and relying on the evidence of PW.1 coupled with documents this court can come to the conclusion that the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident.

13. The unchallenged final report filed by the police clearly establishes negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AB-4003 and in the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

14. In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

sentences.text: With this observation issue No.1 in is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.

4 15. ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AB-4003.

Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16.
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 25 years.
The petitioner has produced the Aadhar card as per Ex.P.9, it disclose the date of birth of the petitioner as 2-5-1997 and the accident took place on 18- 7-2022.
So, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged 25 years.
The petitioner has deposed that prior to the accident he was hale and healthy, working as Electrician under various owners and earning more than Rs.30,000/-p.m..
Due to accidental injuries, he has lost the earnings.
In support of the same petitioner has not produced any documents.

On perusal of the wound certificate marked at Ex.P7,
the petitioner has sustained lacerated wound, blunt injury over the upper and lower limb and the doctor has opined that the said injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.
17. The petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated him to ascertain the percentage of disability suffered by him.
However, on account of the accidental injury the petitioner certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
As per the discharge summary Ex-P10, petitioner has taken treatment at Bangalore Emergency surgical and Trauma care hospital, Bangalore as inpatient for 3 days from 18-7-2022 to 20-7-2022.

entities.text: Bangalore Emergency surgical and Trauma care hospital, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Petitioner has also produced medical bills at Ex.P12 for an amount of Rs.42,151/-, Ex-P13-12 medical prescriptions, Ex-P14-advance receipt for Rs.6,200/-.
The advance receipt of Rs.6,200/- is included in the main medical bill.
Hence advance bill amount of Rs.6,200/- is not taken into consideration.
The injuries suffered by petitioner necessarily caused physical discomforts with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Moreover petitioner would obviously faced depression, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.

18. Hence, taking into consideration of the nature and gravity of the injuries and age and avocation of the petitioner, and the medical expenses spent by him, this tribunal deems fit to award Rs.1,25,000/- as global compensation.
Therefore, petitioner is entitle for global compensation of Rs.1,25,000/-.
19. INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
20. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AB-4003 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'
21.
ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
Manoj vs Subramani on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41309102/
5 O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,25,000=00 with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, the entire amount shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to Stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 2nd day of May 2025).

(Chetana S.F.) IV Addl., Small Cause Judge & ACJM, Court of Small Causes,
Bengaluru.
